skill_description: Best practices for generating and wiring Go HTTP APIs with oapi-codegen (v2), covering strict-server, Gin and Chi integration, validation middleware, auth, project layout, and codegen configuration. Use when adding or regenerating oapi-codegen stubs, choosing gin-server vs chi-server, implementing StrictServerInterface, wiring request validation/auth middleware, writing oapi-codegen YAML config, or reviewing OpenAPI→Go server plumbing.
method: Given only skill name + description (no SKILL.md body), decide load YES/NO for each user message.

cases.prompt: Greenfield Go service: OpenAPI 3 for a pets API. Recommend oapi-codegen (v2) generate config for Gin, how to implement handlers, and how to wire request validation + Bearer auth.
Same pets API but the team standardizes on Chi, not Gin. Give the oapi-codegen config differences and the router wiring, including validation middleware package choice.

Production API returns HTTP 400 with message like 'no matching operation was found' for requests that look valid. Spec has servers with production URLs. App is behind a reverse proxy. Diagnose and fix for an oapi-codegen + validation middleware setup.
StrictServerInterface handler for GET /users/{id}. Domain service returns domain.ErrNotFound or a DB error. How should the handler return 404 vs 500? Show the Go pattern.

Review this plan: hand-edit server.gen.go to rename a type; skip committing generated files; rely on c.ShouldBindJSON in Gin after enabling strict-server; re-enable compatibility.enable-auth-scopes-on-context for new auth. What is wrong?
Only rename an enum description in openapi.yaml for better docs. No paths or schemas change. Do I need oapi-codegen best practices / to regenerate server stubs?
How do I use golang.org/x/sync/errgroup for concurrent TCP health checks with a worker pool limit?
Write better OpenAPI enum naming conventions and examples for our public REST API (string enums, not numeric). No Go code generation discussion.
Add a plain Gin GET /healthz that returns {"status":"ok"}. No OpenAPI, no code generation.
